description: Reusable property shapes for formal-sva contract writing. Placeholders use {{NAME}}. Pick a shape that matches the spec sentence, then replace every placeholder with bundle data and a verbatim spec quote. Do not copy a shape whose meaning is stronger than the sentence.

patterns.name: Reset invariant
patterns.use_when: The spec states the value of an output or register while reset is asserted (active high or low).

fields.expr: Required value while reset is active. Use only constants, ports and resolved parameters; history is forbidden.

template.title: Reset drives {{SIGNAL}} to its specified value

evidence.quote: {{QUOTE}}
While i_rst_n is low, q shall be 4'b0000.

patterns.avoid: Do not add a trigger, prev(), or disable_reset; the kind already scopes itself to reset.

patterns.name: Next-cycle update
patterns.use_when: The spec gives the next value of a registered signal as a function of its current value and inputs.

fields.trigger: Condition at edge t under which the update happens.
fields.expr: Relation that holds at t+1. Refer to the previous value with prev(signal).

evidence.quote: {{QUOTE}}

example.title: An increment below the maximum adds exactly one

evidence.quote: When i_inc is 1 and q is not 15, q shall increment by 1 on the next rising edge of i_clk.

patterns.avoid: Do not use next for combinational outputs: their new value appears in the same cycle. Use always with when.

patterns.name: Hold value
patterns.use_when: The spec says a register or output keeps its value for a cycle when no event occurs.

fields.trigger: Condition under which the value is held.

evidence.quote: {{QUOTE}}

example.title: Without an increment q holds its value

evidence.quote: When i_inc is 0, q shall hold its value on the next rising edge of i_clk.

patterns.avoid: Do not use stability for registered next-state behavior; stability means the signal does not change after a trigger, not that it equals a specified expression.

patterns.name: Unconditional invariant
patterns.use_when: The spec states a condition that must hold on every cycle, independent of any trigger.

fields.expr: Invariant expression over ports and parameters.
fields.when: Optional guard for a mode-specific invariant.

evidence.quote: {{QUOTE}}

example.title: The two grant outputs are never asserted together

evidence.quote: Only one grant output shall be asserted at a time.

patterns.avoid: Do not encode a next-cycle relation here; use next or response.

patterns.name: Qualified invariant
patterns.use_when: The spec states an obligation that applies only when a mode or handshake condition holds, and the obligation is observable in the same cycle.

evidence.quote: {{QUOTE}}

example.title: A read response carries matching data when valid

evidence.quote: When o_rvalid is asserted, o_rlast shall mark the final beat.

patterns.avoid: Do not put a future-cycle obligation in expr; use next or response instead.

patterns.name: Bounded response
patterns.use_when: The spec says that an event must be followed by another event within a number of cycles.

fields.response: Required event at some edge in [t+min_delay, t+max_delay].
fields.min_delay: Minimum delay in clock cycles, at least 1.
fields.max_delay: Maximum delay justified by the spec or interface; must be >= min_delay.

evidence.quote: {{QUOTE}}

example.title: A write request eventually receives a B response

evidence.quote: Every accepted write shall receive a B response within eight clock cycles.

patterns.avoid: Do not claim an unbounded eventually: there is no liveness operator. If the spec gives no bound, choose and document the smallest justified bound, or mark the requirement partially_formalized.

patterns.name: Stable until accepted
patterns.use_when: The spec requires a valid/data payload to remain unchanged until the handshake completes.

fields.trigger: Valid asserted and not yet accepted (e.g. valid && !ready).
fields.signal: Payload or control signal that must not change.
fields.cycles: Number of following edges over which it must stay stable.

evidence.quote: {{QUOTE}}

example.title: AW payload stays stable until AW is accepted

evidence.quote: Once i_awvalid is asserted, i_awaddr shall remain stable until o_awready.

patterns.avoid: If the sentence constrains an input protocol, this is an assumption, not an assertion: use role assume. Do not use stability for a register's next-state function.

patterns.name: Reachability cover
patterns.use_when: A scenario, trigger, mode or boundary condition must be reachable; or an assertion would otherwise be vacuous.

fields.expr: Condition that must be reachable after reset.
fields.severity: info unless the spec requires the scenario to exist.

evidence.quote: {{QUOTE}}

example.title: An increment at zero is reachable after reset

evidence.quote: A cycle with i_inc 1 and q 0 shall be reachable after reset.

patterns.avoid: Do not use role assert with kind cover, and do not set severity error unless the spec demands the scenario occur in every run.

patterns.name: Environment stability assumption
patterns.use_when: The spec constrains an input protocol that the environment must obey, such as input payload stability.

fields.when: Guard: the protocol condition under which the constraint applies.
fields.expr: Constraint on input signals, usually stable(input) or a relation between inputs.

evidence.quote: {{QUOTE}}

example.title: The host holds AW payload while AW is pending

evidence.quote: The host shall keep i_awaddr stable while i_awvalid is asserted and o_awready is low.

patterns.avoid: Never assume a DUT output, and never assume the behavior a requirement asks the DUT to provide. Guard the assumption; an unguarded assume constrains every cycle.

patterns.name: Environment valid/payload assumption
patterns.use_when: The spec defines when an input payload is meaningful, e.g. data is only valid with valid asserted.

fields.expr: Relation between input valid and its payload, or a onehot/range constraint on inputs.

evidence.quote: {{QUOTE}}

example.title: At most one read request is presented

evidence.quote: The host shall not assert i_arvalid and i_awvalid in the same cycle.

patterns.avoid: Do not assume parameter values; they are resolved at render time. Do not use onehot on a multi-bit payload unless the spec says so.

patterns.name: No response without request
patterns.use_when: The spec forbids an output from asserting unless a corresponding request or enable occurred.

fields.expr: output -> request (use prev(...) when the request is one cycle earlier).

evidence.quote: {{QUOTE}}

example.title: A B response is asserted only after a write was accepted

evidence.quote: o_bvalid shall be asserted only in response to an accepted write.

patterns.avoid: Do not use prev() on the output being checked; prev() is for the earlier request. Do not add this pattern if the spec allows unsolicited responses.

patterns.name: Parameter boundary case
patterns.use_when: The spec defines behavior at a parameter-dependent boundary (maximum, wrap, zero, all-ones).

fields.trigger: Condition at the boundary, written with the resolved parameter.
fields.expr: Required boundary value or wrap relation.

evidence.quote: {{QUOTE}}

example.title: An increment at the maximum wraps to zero

evidence.quote: When i_inc is 1 and q is 15, q shall wrap to 0 on the next rising edge of i_clk.

patterns.avoid: Do not hard-code a value that the spec states in terms of a parameter. Parameters are resolved to integers at render time, so the same contract checks the configured instance only.
